etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English membre, from Old French membre, from Latin membrum (“limb, body part”), from Proto-Italic *memzrom, from Proto-Indo-European *mḗms, *mēms-rom (“flesh”). Akin to Gothic 𐌼𐌹𐌼𐌶 (mimz, “meat, flesh”), Crimean Gothic menus.

Coexists with native Middle English lim, limb (“member, limb, joint”) (from Old English lim (“limb, joint, main branch”)), and displaced Middle English lith (“limb, joint, member”) (from Old English liþ (“limb, member, join, tip”)).

definitions.definition: One who belongs to a group.

quote.citation: 2014 January 14, Roberta Rogow, The Problem of the Surly Servant‎[1], →ISBN, page 109:
quote.text: “Were it not for the fancy French and Latin in it, I'd have swore it was the sort of thing I do not print as a rule, but being as how the order was from one of the members upstairs...”

quote.citation: 1979, Kenneth J. Englund, "The Mississippian and Pennsylvanian (Carbonfierous) Systems in the United States - Virginia", Page C-14, in Geological Survey Professional Paper, Volume 1110
quote.text: The member intertongues and grades laterally with the lower sandstone member of the Pocahontas Formation of Early Pennslyvanian age

definitions.definition: Part of an animal capable of performing a distinct office; an organ; a limb.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Romans 12:4:
quote.text: For as we haue many members in one body, and all members haue not the same office:

definitions.definition: (logic) One of the propositions making up a syllogism.
(set theory) An element of a set.
(Australia, law) the judge or adjudicator in a consumer court.
A part of a discourse or of a period, sentence, or verse; a clause.
(mathematics) Either of the two parts of an algebraic equation, connected by the equality sign.
(computing) A file stored within an archive file.
(object-oriented programming) A function or piece of data associated with each separate instance of a class.
(obsolete outside dialects) Pronunciation spelling of remember.
